title.narrative: A Comprehensive GBV Response through Case Management, Psychosocial Support and Empowerment Services in targeted woredas of Mao Komo and Bulen woredas of Beninshangul Gumuz.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed action will be implemented in targeted woredas of Beninshangul Gumuz Region (BGRS) (Bulen woreda of Metekel zone and Mao Komo Special woreda) with the aim of enhancing protection, resilience, and dignity for GBV survivors while strengthening local systems for long-term impact through provision of technical support for local organizations and government sectors. The action will ensure age- and gender-responsive approaches by employing participatory assessments to customize interventions to the various needs of women, girls, and other vulnerable populations. Implementation will be guided by a do-no-harm framework and strong feedback mechanisms, guaranteeing safety, and accountability.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe International Rescue Committee (IRC) aims to empower women and girls in conflict-affected areas to lead safer and more resilient lives by improving access to protection services, promoting their active participation in decision-making. It also focuses on improving access to survivor-centered case management, mental health and psychosocial support, timely referrals to specialized services, and the distribution of dignity kits and emergency cash assistance. The establishment of Women and Girls Friendly Spaces (WGFS) and strengthening of One-Stop Centers (OSCs) will provide safe environments and integrated services. Community awareness campaigns will help prevent GBV and promote access to support.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe project will target affected community members to address the critical needs of GBV survivors including FGM, preventing further deterioration of the situation and mitigating immediate and long-term impacts on the affected people. The selection of beneficiaries will be guided by a transparent, inclusive, and needs-based approach, prioritizing the most vulnerable populations, including women-headed households, persons with disabilities, the elderly, and internally displaced persons. Community engagement will be central to the process, with initial targeting informed by multi-sectoral needs assessments and validated through participatory community consultations. Selection criteria will be clearly communicated to all stakeholders to ensure fairness and accountability. A robust feedback and complaints mechanism will be established, including suggestion boxes, and a dedicated hotline, enabling beneficiaries to voice concerns, provide input, and report compliances confidentially. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe proposed action will also complement ongoing EHF projects where relevant and ensure operational coordination and programmatic synergies among the partners funded to implement GBV prevention and response services in the targeted woredas.ltbrgtlt/pgt
